Video Games are about selling you fantasies. Stories. Fun.

And in recent years, we've been seeing a trend - video games should be about more than that. Video games have become, on occasion, platforms for social issues. Okay - I'll grant that video games, tastefully done, can be about greater things than just fun. And it's a nice direction to take them in - Sounds like what Shakespeare did to English theatre. Fundamentally, at least, it was a good idea.

Except that most game-developers who try to present social issues are not Shakespeare. Most of the video games that present social issues are, to be frank, not as able to present a good game. And the gaming press is willing to misreport on the failings of these games, because they carry a meaning that the press feels is more important than the game itself.

Look, I understand that social issues are important. However, in the context of a video game, the message you try to push should not take precedence over the game itself. Just like how in art, the message behind the piece of art should not be more important than the beauty of the artwork itself.

In that sense, I think that the gaming press should report objectively on the triumphs and failings of certain games, and not be swayed in favour of certain games just because of the messages behind them.

But more than that - there's a dangerous ideology being spread by feminists such as Anita Sarkeesian, who lacks an unbiased understanding of the video games they criticize. Yes, it's true that, in some video games, women are given a lower status than men - but again, there's a justifiable reason to do so. It's because the video games are trying to tell you a story, to give you a setting - this is a misogynistic world. This does not mean that the developer is justifying that world's misogyny in any way - misogyny's simply part of the setting. To say that video games with misogynistic elements promote misogyny would be similar to saying that George Orwell's 1984 promotes governmental surveillance. On the contrary, the misogyny is often there to help present the idea that the world in the video game is not an ideal world.

And feminists who criticize video games don't necessarily understand this - nor do others who watch their videos. And I think, personally, that Gamergate is a valid movement that is trying to re-assess these wrongs. Video games should be about fun, first and foremost - social commentary can have a place in games, but if the game itself is poorly done, then the fact that it contains social commentary shouldn't be enough to push it to get 5 star reviews. Similarly, just because video games contain sexist content, it doesn't mean that they're promoting sexism. Gamergate's original grievances were perfectly legitimate - and given that these grievances were left unaddressed till now, they're still all the more legitimate.
